subject: Decommissioning backup snapshot window & temporary log-retention exception
messages:
From: James Porter <james.porter@acme-health.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com
Date: 2028-06-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Backup decommissioning timeline + short log retention exception request

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. Were preparing to retire the legacy EBS-backed snapshots that contain PII we previously ingested for a one-off migration. Legal is asking for a clear purge timetable and confirmation of what remains in system logs before we sign off. Two asks from our side:

1) A proposed schedule for when backups tied to Acme Health will be irreversibly deleted (including copies held by subprocessors).
2) A short-term exception to keep audit log entries for 90 days (instead of our default 30) while Acme finishes an internal validation sweep. That exception needs a traceable justification and owner.

I've attached an excerpt of the data inventory (acme_data_inventory.csv) — it flags which datasets are in the snapshots. Can you confirm the high-level plan and whether we need a DPA amendment or a simple confirmation note?

Best,
James Porter
Senior IT Compliance Manager
Acme Health
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
To: James Porter <james.porter@acme-health.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-20T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Backup decommissioning timeline + short log retention exception request

James —

Thanks for the inventory extract — that helps. Quick summary of our proposed approach:

- Backup purge timetable: We can schedule irreversible deletion of the snapshot corpus containing Acme data on 2028-07-15, with a pre-delete 7-day notification window (2028-07-08 to 2028-07-15) to allow any final appeals.
- Subprocessor copies: We will coordinate with our backup storage subprocessor (CloudStore Ops) to confirm copies are purged within 48 hours of our deletion action; we will request written confirmation.
- Log retention exception: We can grant a temporary extension to 90 days for Acme-specific audit logs, scoped to the minimal set of event types you specify (access/authn events + snapshot lifecycle entries). This will be time-limited: 90 days from the effective date of the exception.

Two compliance notes:
1) If the extension materially changes our data processing scope, legal will want a short DPA amendment (one paragraph + effective window).
2) We will record the exception as an internal policy waiver with a named owner on our side (I propose Karthik as owner for ops coordination).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to confirm operational feasibility and whether CloudStore Ops needs a separate ticket.
- Kimberly to check whether the exception triggers any regulatory notification we must add to the DPA.
- We will draft a one-paragraph DPA amendment if required, circulate for signature, and provide an evidence packet (confirmation from CloudStore + deletion job run logs).

Attaching a proposed one-pager for the internal waiver and the DPA amendment template.

Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-20T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Backup decommissioning timeline + short log retention exception request

Hannah / Kimberly —

Operational check: we can do the 2028-07-15 irreversible purge date. Notes:

- CloudStore Ops will need a ticket cut by 2028-06-28 to schedule the remove job and to snapshot the current KV for audit; otherwise their SLA pushes the job out by two weeks.
- For subprocessor purges: some long-tail replicas exist in our cross-region cold tier. Those are controlled by CloudStore and will take up to 48 hours after our deletion trigger; we will request and attach their job IDs.
- Log extension: to avoid preserving full payloads, we suggest scoping to event metadata only (timestamp, user-id hash, event-type, snapshot-id). That keeps PII off logs while still giving Acme the visibility they need.

Action items for this thread:
- Kimberly: confirm if we can scope logs as above without requiring a formal DPA amendment.
- Laura: can you pre-write the CloudStore confirmation template so procurement can accept it as evidence?

Ill create the CloudStore ticket once we have the formal sign-off window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Systems Engineer, Inference Ops
From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: James Porter <james.porter@acme-health.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-21T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Backup decommissioning timeline + short log retention exception request

James —

Appreciate the clear ask. Legal reviewed Karthiks scoping suggestion and we can handle this two ways:

Option A (preferred, faster): A signed confirmation note plus the CloudStore job confirmation and deletion logs. No DPA text change needed because we are not changing the types of data processed, only the retention window for specific logs. The confirmation will include: scope, owner, effective window (90 days), and evidence requirements.

Option B (more formal): A one-paragraph DPA amendment that explicitly enumerates the temporary 90-day log-retention exception. This adds time (signature routing) but may be what your procurement team prefers.

Given procurement/Legal at Acme often require explicit amendments for retention terms, I recommend we prepare the quick confirmation note and the DPA paragraph in parallel so you can choose. Laura, please attach the CloudStore confirmation template and the internal waiver.

James, if you confirm Option A is acceptable, well:
- Cut CloudStore ticket by 2028-06-28
- Lock the purge date to 2028-07-15 with 7d notice
- Provide deletion job IDs and the limited audit log export (metadata-only) once complete

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
